2a28fe841d59.domanda: What does the acronym DBMS stand for?
2a28fe841d59.spiegazione: DBMS stands for DataBase Management System. It is the software that sits between applications and physical data, ensuring integrity, concurrency, recovery, and access control.
risposte: Data Binary Mapping Schema
Distributed Base Model Server
DataBase Management System
Dynamic Block Memory Storage

8a10daa0e7ac.domanda: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental requirement of a database?
8a10daa0e7ac.spiegazione: The three fundamental requirements are: minimal data redundancy, concurrent access, and persistence/durability. Maximum insertion speed is not a defining requirement: it is balanced with integrity and security.
risposte: Minimal data redundancy
Concurrent access by multiple users simultaneously connected to the same shared database
Guaranteed maximum insertion speed in all circumstances
Data persistence and durability

34384a498b72.domanda: Who proposed the relational model in 1970?
34384a498b72.spiegazione: Edgar F. Codd proposed the relational model in 1970 at the IBM San Jose Research Laboratory, based on the mathematical theory of relations between sets.
risposte: Edgar F. Codd
Bill Gates
Donald Chamberlin
Charles Bachman

d592397ddb24.domanda: What are metadata in a database?
d592397ddb24.spiegazione: Metadata (data about data) describe the structure of the database: column names, allowed data types, constraints. They are distinct from the actual data, which represents the entities of the system.
risposte: Duplicate data for security on a backup server
Structures that describe how data is organized: column names, data types, constraints
Automatic backups generated by the DBMS
Queries saved as VIEWs in the database

43a47b3e8c96.domanda: What is the main advantage of data independence in a DBMS?
43a47b3e8c96.spiegazione: Data independence means that applications are unaware of the physical structure. You can add a column or move data to another disk without rewriting the programs that use it.
risposte: Queries are executed automatically in parallel
Data is automatically encrypted on disk without any additional configuration by the user
Each user has their own local copy of the data
You can change the physical structure of the data without having to rewrite the applications

763a77ff9f0f.domanda: Which of these is an example of a NoSQL database?
763a77ff9f0f.spiegazione: MongoDB is a document-based NoSQL database. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle are relational databases that use SQL. NoSQL databases emerged in the 2000s to manage large volumes of unstructured data.
risposte: PostgreSQL
MySQL
Oracle Database
MongoDB

8769b651aee4.domanda: In the relational model, what does a 'row' (row/tuple) represent?
8769b651aee4.spiegazione: A row (also called a tuple or record) represents a specific instance of the entity: a concrete customer, a real product, a specific order. Columns describe its properties.
risposte: A specific instance of the entity: a concrete object such as a customer or a product
A property of the entity with its data type
The complete and detailed structure of the table, including column names and all constraints
The set of all possible values for a column

cf837eec77fb.domanda: What is the 'domain' of a column in the relational model?
cf837eec77fb.spiegazione: The domain is the set of permissible values for a column. It is defined by the data type (INT, VARCHAR, DATE...) combined with any CHECK constraints. E.g., an age column with type INT and CHECK (age >= 0 AND age <= 130).
risposte: The name of the database to which the table belongs
The maximum number of rows the table can contain
The set of permissible values for that column, defined by the data type and CHECK constraints
The maximum number of characters for text-type columns

ada3ca1c9b60.spiegazione: A natural key is an attribute that is already meaningful in the real-world domain and identifies the entity (e.g., tax code for a person, ISBN for a book). An artificial key (surrogate key), on the other hand, is added specifically without real-world meaning, such as a SERIAL sequential number.
risposte: An artificial key generated automatically as SERIAL or UUID
An attribute added specifically to the table, completely devoid of meaning in the real-world domain
An attribute already present in the entity that naturally identifies it (e.g., tax code, ISBN)
A key composed of two or more columns

604c60e24278.domanda: What differentiates the 'schema' from the 'instance' of a table?
604c60e24278.spiegazione: The schema defines the table structure (columns, types, constraints) and is stable over time. The instance is the current content (the rows present) and changes continuously with DML operations.
risposte: The schema is the current content of the rows; the instance is the structure of the columns
The schema is the stable structure (column names, types, constraints); the instance is the current content that changes with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
Schema and instance are interchangeable synonyms in SQL
The schema changes with every INSERT; the instance remains unchanged

cd5150d3d81f.domanda: In which type of relationship between entities can a row in table A be associated with multiple rows in B and vice versa?
cd5150d3d81f.spiegazione: The N:N (many-to-many) relationship is the one where entity A can be associated with multiple entities B and vice versa. Example: a student can enroll in multiple courses, and a course can have multiple students. It is implemented using a junction table.
risposte: 1:1 (one-to-one)
1:N (one-to-many)
N:1 (many-to-one)
N:N (many-to-many)

42b8f8242e4a.domanda: Why is a surrogate key often preferred over a natural key?
42b8f8242e4a.spiegazione: Natural keys can change (e.g., a tax code may be corrected) or cause issues (reassigned acronyms, duplicates across different systems). A surrogate key (SERIAL, UUID) is stable, has no meaning in the real-world domain, and does not depend on external rules.
risposte: Because it is necessarily of type UUID and therefore universally unique globally across every system
Because it always takes up significantly less disk space than any possible composite natural key
Because it is more stable over time: it does not change meaning and does not depend on external rules
Because natural keys are in no way supported by the SQL standard or by the main DBMS in use

4eb76d6db06e.domanda: What happens by default (without CASCADE options) if you attempt to delete a parent record that has child rows linked via a FOREIGN KEY?
4eb76d6db06e.spiegazione: The default behavior is RESTRICT: the DBMS prevents the deletion of the parent if there are child rows referencing it, returning an error. To achieve different behaviors, you specify ON DELETE CASCADE, ON DELETE SET NULL, etc.
risposte: The parent is deleted and the child rows are set to NULL
The parent is deleted and the child rows are deleted automatically in a cascade
The DBMS blocks the operation with a referential integrity violation error
The parent is deleted and the child rows remain unchanged (dangling references)

af47d023e3ef.domanda: Why can't duplicate rows exist in the relational model?
af47d023e3ef.spiegazione: From a mathematical perspective, a relation (table) is a set of tuples. Sets, by definition, do not contain duplicate elements. The PRIMARY KEY is the practical mechanism that implements this mathematical property.
risposte: Because the SQL engine immediately returns a blocking syntax error whenever a duplicate row is attempted to be inserted
Because mathematically a table is a set, and sets do not contain duplicate elements
Because the DBMS automatically sorts rows and removes duplicates
Because the PRIMARY KEY is always mandatory by SQL standard law

a5de9bfdba60.spiegazione: 1NF requires that each cell contains an atomic value (not divisible into smaller parts with independent meaning) and that there are no repeating groups. For example, a 'phones' column containing multiple numbers in a single string violates 1NF.
risposte: All non-key attributes are fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key of the table
Each column contains atomic (indivisible) values and there are no repeating groups of columns
There are no transitive dependencies between non-key attributes
The table has exactly one column defined as NOT NULL

e397947923dc.domanda: What is the Second Normal Form (2NF)?
e397947923dc.spiegazione: 2NF requires that the table is in 1NF and that every non-key attribute is functionally dependent on the entire primary key. If the PK is composite and an attribute depends only on part of it (partial dependency), 2NF is violated.
risposte: The table is in 1NF and all non-key attributes depend on the entire primary key (no partial dependencies)
The table has no multi-valued attributes in columns
There are no transitive dependencies between non-key attributes
The table has at least three columns that form the composite primary key
The table is in 1NF and there are no repeated attributes in any column
The table is in 2NF and there are no transitive dependencies: no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute
The table has at least three foreign keys to other tables
The table never uses JOINs with more than three tables in any query
c2518cd04fb3.spiegazione: 3NF requires the table to be in 2NF and to have no transitive dependencies: no non-key attribute may depend on another non-key attribute (only on the primary key). E.g.: if cap determines citta, and citta is a non-key attribute, there is a transitive dependency.

dbb5b1a32a1d.domanda: Which anomaly occurs when updating redundant data modifies it only in some rows, creating inconsistency?
dbb5b1a32a1d.spiegazione: An update anomaly occurs when the same information is stored in multiple rows and is updated in only some of them, causing contradictory data. Normalization eliminates this redundancy by storing each fact only once.
risposte: Insertion anomaly
Deletion anomaly
Update anomaly
Projection anomaly

acd957500e86.domanda: A table with a 'phones' column containing '333-111, 333-222, 333-333' in a single purple cell violates which normal form?
acd957500e86.spiegazione: First Normal Form (1NF) requires atomic values: each cell must contain a single indivisible value. A cell containing multiple phone numbers separated by commas violates 1NF. The solution is to create a separate 'phones' table with one row for each number.
risposte: 2NF — partial dependency on the key
3NF — presence of a transitive dependency between two non-key attributes of the same table
1NF — the value is not atomic (contains multiple numbers in a single cell)
Does not violate any normal form

d1b6f3925000.domanda: What is the primary purpose of database normalization?
d1b6f3925000.spiegazione: Normalization aims to eliminate redundancy and design a relational schema that avoids anomalies. Note: normalization can reduce query performance (more JOINs required); in some cases, denormalization is intentionally applied to optimize.
risposte: A. Increase the read speed of SELECT queries
B. Reduce redundancy and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies
C. Increase the number of tables to distribute the server load
D. Make the database accessible exclusively to users with specific, properly granted permissions

41a4287bfcb2.domanda: Which SQL command belongs to DDL and creates a new table?
41a4287bfcb2.spiegazione: CREATE TABLE is the DDL (Data Definition Language) command for creating a new table. DDL includes CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE: commands that define or modify the database structure, not the data.
risposte: INSERT TABLE nome (...);
NEW TABLE nome (...);
ADD TABLE nome (...);
CREATE TABLE nome (...);

315932cd8f5a.domanda: Which DDL command modifies the structure of an existing table?
315932cd8f5a.spiegazione: ALTER TABLE allows you to add/remove columns, change data types, rename columns, add or remove constraints. Example: ALTER TABLE books ADD genre VARCHAR(50);
risposte: MODIFY TABLE
UPDATE TABLE
ALTER TABLE
CHANGE TABLE

3f8b6017a58a.domanda: What does DROP TABLE name CASCADE do?
3f8b6017a58a.spiegazione: DROP TABLE name CASCADE drops the table and, cascadingly, all dependent objects: the VIEWS that use it, and the FOREIGN KEYs from other tables that reference it. Without CASCADE, if dependencies exist, the command returns an error (RESTRICT behavior).
risposte: Deletes the table only if it is completely empty
Deletes the table and all objects (VIEWS, FOREIGN KEYs) that depend on it
Deletes the data but keeps the table structure
Deletes the table only if it has no incoming foreign key constraints

1dc8ceeaa577.domanda: What is the main difference between DELETE FROM table (without WHERE) and TRUNCATE TABLE table?
1dc8ceeaa577.spiegazione: TRUNCATE empties the table without logging each individual deleted row in the transaction log, making it much faster on large tables. Both preserve the table structure. TRUNCATE with RESTART IDENTITY also resets SERIAL counters.
risposte: DELETE is faster; TRUNCATE is slower and safer
TRUNCATE is faster because it does not log each row in the transaction log; DELETE logs all of them
DELETE preserves the table structure; TRUNCATE deletes it along with the data
There is no practical difference between the two: they produce exactly the same result with the same performance

7391bb706813.domanda: What does ALTER TABLE libri ADD genere VARCHAR(50) do?
7391bb706813.spiegazione: ALTER TABLE ... ADD adds a new column to the table. The new column will be populated with NULL for all existing rows, unless a DEFAULT is specified.
risposte: Deletes the 'genere' column from the libri table
Renames the existing column to 'genere'
Adds a new 'genere' column of type VARCHAR(50) to the libri table
Changes the data type of the existing 'genere' column to VARCHAR(50)

5840a35ba7c5.domanda: What does an INDEX do in SQL?
5840a35ba7c5.spiegazione: An index speeds up search operations (SELECT with WHERE, ORDER BY, JOIN) by allowing the DBMS to locate rows without scanning the entire table. The trade-off is that INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations become slightly slower because the index must be updated.
risposte: Speeds up search queries on columns frequently used in WHERE and JOIN clauses, at the expense of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE performance
Guarantees uniqueness of values in a column
Creates an automatic backup of the table on disk
Links two tables with an automatic foreign key

76e1e2744f4b.domanda: Which data type is used in PostgreSQL for a column with an auto-incrementing integer value (primary key)?
76e1e2744f4b.spiegazione: In PostgreSQL, SERIAL is the type (shorthand) for an integer column with an auto-incrementing sequence. It is equivalent to INT DEFAULT nextval('sequence'). In recent SQL standard, GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY is used.
risposte: AUTOINCREMENT INT
IDENTITY(1,1)
SERIAL
AUTO_INCREMENT

1fc35bbe6701.domanda: What does DROP TABLE IF EXISTS name do?
1fc35bbe6701.spiegazione: IF EXISTS is a safety modifier: if the table does not exist, the command terminates without error instead of raising an exception. Useful in setup scripts where it is not certain whether the table exists.
risposte: Deletes the table and returns an error if it does not exist
Deletes the table only if it is empty, otherwise returns an error
Deletes the table if it exists, without error if it does not exist
Checks for the existence of the table without deleting it

32c0d1aa17e3.domanda: What is a SCHEMA in PostgreSQL?
32c0d1aa17e3.spiegazione: A schema is a logical namespace within a database that groups tables, VIEWS, and other objects. It allows organizing objects and managing permissions in a granular manner. The default schema in PostgreSQL is called 'public'.
risposte: A database configuration file saved to disk
A namespace (logical container) that organizes tables within a database
The physical structure of data files on the filesystem
It is a special type of index reserved exclusively for primary key columns

819f1a19ba14.domanda: Which ALTER TABLE clause renames a column in PostgreSQL?
819f1a19ba14.spiegazione: The correct syntax in PostgreSQL is: ALTER TABLE table_name RENAME COLUMN old_name TO new_name; To rename the table itself, use: ALTER TABLE name RENAME TO new_name;
risposte: ALTER COLUMN old TO new
CHANGE COLUMN old new
MODIFY COLUMN old AS new
RENAME COLUMN old TO new

9c7a1dfabf6b.domanda: How does a UNIQUE INDEX created on a column differ from a regular INDEX?
9c7a1dfabf6b.spiegazione: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX creates an index that, in addition to speeding up searches, ensures that all values in the indexed column (or combination of columns) are unique. It is an alternative to the UNIQUE constraint defined on the table.
risposte: The UNIQUE INDEX is faster for searches
The UNIQUE INDEX prevents the insertion of duplicate values in that column, in addition to speeding up searches
The UNIQUE INDEX physically sorts the data on disk
The UNIQUE INDEX replaces the PRIMARY KEY

6061f42bd2c8.domanda: What does ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN col TYPE SMALLINT do?
6061f42bd2c8.spiegazione: ALTER COLUMN col TYPE new_type modifies the data type of an existing column. The DBMS attempts to convert existing values: if the conversion is not possible (e.g., non-convertible text to an integer), it returns an error.
risposte: Adds a CHECK constraint to the column that limits the allowed value to the range permitted by SMALLINT
Changes the data type of column col from its current type to SMALLINT
Simply renames column col to the new name SMALLINT without changing its type
Creates a new optimized SMALLINT index on column col to speed up searches

b3dbd6e3a284.domanda: Which DML command inserts new data into a table?
b3dbd6e3a284.spiegazione: INSERT INTO is the DML command for inserting new records. It is good practice to always specify the column list (INSERT INTO t (col1, col2) VALUES ...) to make the code robust against future changes to the table structure.
risposte: INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values);
ADD INTO table (columns) VALUES (values);
PUT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values);
APPEND INTO table (columns) VALUES (values);

604cd27be5da.domanda: What happens if you execute UPDATE libri SET prezzo = 0 without the WHERE clause?
604cd27be5da.spiegazione: Without WHERE, UPDATE modifies ALL rows in the table. There is no syntax error, but the effect can be disastrous. Best practice: run a SELECT with the same condition first to verify which rows will be modified.
risposte: The command immediately returns a syntax error, because the WHERE clause is mandatory in UPDATE
Only the first row in physical order of the table is updated, setting the price to 0
All rows in the libri table are updated with prezzo = 0
The DBMS always asks for explicit confirmation from the user before proceeding with the update

1fe06f20a4b5.domanda: Which PostgreSQL (non-standard SQL) clause returns the values of the rows just inserted, modified, or deleted?
1fe06f20a4b5.spiegazione: RETURNING is a PostgreSQL clause that returns the values of the rows just affected. It is useful for retrieving the auto-generated ID from a SERIAL column after an INSERT, without needing to perform a second SELECT.
risposte: OUTPUT
RESULT
ECHO
RETURNING

655be8777662.domanda: What is the correct syntax to insert multiple rows with a single INSERT?
655be8777662.spiegazione: Multiple INSERT uses a comma-separated list of values: INSERT INTO t (col1, col2) VALUES (1,'A'), (2,'B'), (3,'C'); It is much more efficient than separate INSERTs because it reduces the number of round-trips with the database.
risposte: INSERT MULTIPLE INTO t VALUES (1,'A'),(2,'B');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,'A'), (2,'B');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,'A'); INSERT INTO t VALUES (2,'B');
INSERT INTO t ROWS (1,'A'),(2,'B');

d562cf92180b.domanda: How do you update two columns simultaneously with a single UPDATE statement?
d562cf92180b.spiegazione: In the SET clause of an UPDATE statement, multiple assignments must be separated by commas: SET col1=v1, col2=v2. The AND operator is not used (it is a logical operator for WHERE), nor is SET repeated.
risposte: UPDATE t SET col1=v1 AND col2=v2 WHERE cond;
UPDATE t SET col1=v1 SET col2=v2 WHERE cond;
UPDATE t SET col1=v1, col2=v2 WHERE cond;
UPDATE t MODIFY col1=v1, col2=v2 WHERE cond;

1c2e63c4cf22.domanda: What does the INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... statement allow you to do?
1c2e63c4cf22.spiegazione: INSERT INTO destination_table (col1, col2) SELECT col1, col2 FROM source_table WHERE condition; allows you to copy data from one table to another in a single operation. Useful for archiving or migrating data.
risposte: Automatically create a new table with the structure and data returned by a SELECT query
Update existing rows using data read row by row from another source table
Insert data read from another table (or query) without having to list it manually
Create a permanent VIEW based on a SELECT query, assigning it a reusable name

b8283cc080d1.domanda: Why is it recommended to explicitly specify columns in an INSERT statement?
b8283cc080d1.spiegazione: INSERT INTO t VALUES (...) without a column list requires that the values match the exact and complete order of the table definition. If a column is added to the table, all such INSERT statements will break. Specifying the columns makes the code resilient to schema changes.
risposte: Because, without an explicit column list, the INSERT statement is not compiled by any existing DBMS
For clarity and robustness: if a column is added to the table in the future, the INSERT remains valid
Because it is the only way to insert NULL values into a column
Because it significantly speeds up the insertion operation

0d0bf76e7fc0.domanda: What does DELETE FROM libri WHERE anno < 1900 do?
0d0bf76e7fc0.spiegazione: DELETE FROM table WHERE condition physically removes from the database all rows that satisfy the condition. The operation is irreversible (unless ROLLBACK is performed within a transaction). It does not select or update: it deletes.
risposte: Updates by setting to NULL the values of the anno column in all rows where anno is less than 1900
Selects and displays only the rows where anno is less than 1900, without modifying them in any way
Deletes from the libri table all rows where the anno column is less than 1900
Automatically moves the rows where anno is less than 1900 into a dedicated archive table

e92c8c827533.domanda: Which SQL constraint ensures that a column cannot contain NULL values?
e92c8c827533.spiegazione: NOT NULL is the constraint that requires every row to provide a non-null value for that column. It is different from UNIQUE (which ensures the absence of duplicates) and from PRIMARY KEY (which implies both NOT NULL and UNIQUE).
risposte: UNIQUE
CHECK
NOT NULL
REQUIRED

238c50923dbe.domanda: What does a CHECK constraint on a column do?
238c50923dbe.spiegazione: CHECK allows defining an arbitrary validation rule. E.g., CHECK (age >= 0 AND age <= 130), CHECK (price >= 0), CHECK (status IN ('active','inactive')). The DBMS rejects any INSERT or UPDATE that violates the condition.
risposte: Verifies that the inserted value satisfies a logical condition specified by the developer
Verifies that the value is not duplicated in the table
Verifies that the value is not NULL
Verifies that the inserted value corresponds to a valid foreign key already present in another linked table

9b9afd114111.domanda: What does ON DELETE CASCADE do on a FOREIGN KEY?
9b9afd114111.spiegazione: ON DELETE CASCADE automatically deletes child rows when the parent is deleted. It is useful for strong dependency relationships (e.g., deleting an author also deletes all their books). Use with caution to avoid unexpected cascading deletions.
risposte: Prevents deletion of the parent record if child rows exist
Sets the FK column of child rows to NULL when the parent is deleted
Automatically deletes child rows when the parent record is deleted
Sets the FK of child rows to the DEFAULT value when the parent is deleted

b6acb4d3a250.domanda: How many PRIMARY KEYs can a single table have?
b6acb4d3a250.spiegazione: Each table can have exactly one PRIMARY KEY. However, it can be composed of multiple columns (a composite primary key). PRIMARY KEY implies NOT NULL + UNIQUE on all columns that make it up.
risposte: No precise limit: it allows one for each column declared NOT NULL
At most two keys: one of simple type and one of composite type made up of multiple columns
Only one (even if it can be composed of multiple columns)
At most three primary keys, as specified by the most recent SQL standard

144bd0e4e723.domanda: What is the difference between PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE as constraints?
144bd0e4e723.spiegazione: PRIMARY KEY implies NOT NULL + UNIQUE. UNIQUE guarantees uniqueness but allows NULL (in PostgreSQL, multiple rows can have NULL in a UNIQUE column, because NULL is not equal to NULL). A table can have only one PK but multiple UNIQUE constraints.
risposte: PRIMARY KEY allows NULL; UNIQUE does not
UNIQUE allows NULL (in PostgreSQL, multiple NULLs are also allowed); PRIMARY KEY never allows NULL
PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE are completely identical: both guarantee both uniqueness and non-nullability of values
PRIMARY KEY allows duplicates; UNIQUE does not

7a40e4da0968.domanda: What does the DEFAULT constraint do on a column?
7a40e4da0968.spiegazione: DEFAULT provides a preset value for the column when the INSERT statement does not specify one. Examples: DEFAULT 0, DEFAULT 'available', DEFAULT TRUE, DEFAULT NOW() (current timestamp). The column can still explicitly receive NULL unless it is also defined as NOT NULL.
risposte: Prevents the insertion of NULL values into that column
Verifies that the value is within a defined range
Sets an automatic value when an INSERT does not specify a value for that column
Sets the value as the primary key of the table

928b65ddb4c2.domanda: How do you add a FOREIGN KEY constraint to an existing table?
928b65ddb4c2.spiegazione: ALTER TABLE with ADD CONSTRAINT is used to add any constraint to an existing table: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK. Named constraints (CONSTRAINT nome ...) can later be removed with ALTER TABLE t DROP CONSTRAINT nome.
risposte: CREATE FOREIGN KEY ON table (col) REFERENCES other(pk) ON DELETE CASCADE NOT NULL;
INSERT CONSTRAINT FOREIGN KEY INTO table (col) REFERENCES other (pk) ON UPDATE RESTRICT;
MODIFY TABLE table ADD FOREIGN KEY (col) REFERENCES other(pk) ON DELETE SET NULL;
ALTER TABLE table ADD CONSTRAINT name FOREIGN KEY (col) REFERENCES other(pk);

e764661a0b20.domanda: What does ON DELETE SET NULL do on a FOREIGN KEY?
e764661a0b20.spiegazione: ON DELETE SET NULL sets the FK column of child rows to NULL when the parent record is deleted. It requires the FK column to be defined as nullable (without NOT NULL). Alternative: ON DELETE SET DEFAULT uses the column's default value.
risposte: Blocks the deletion of the parent if child rows exist
Sets the FK column of the child row to NULL when the parent is deleted
Deletes child rows along with the parent
Sets the FK column to its predefined DEFAULT value whenever the parent record is deleted

b3c9c2f46676.domanda: What does the DISTINCT keyword do in a SELECT statement?
b3c9c2f46676.spiegazione: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result set. Note: it operates on all columns in the SELECT combined. SELECT DISTINCT col1, col2 returns unique combinations of (col1, col2), not the unique values of each column separately.
risposte: Automatically sorts rows in descending order based on the values in the first column
Removes from the final query result all rows that contain at least one NULL value
Returns only rows with distinct values, removing duplicates
Selects and returns only the rows that satisfy a specific boolean condition indicated

eb91c9f38266.domanda: Which SQL clause orders the result of a query?
eb91c9f38266.spiegazione: ORDER BY sorts the query result. By default, the order is ASC (ascending). Use DESC for descending order. Multiple columns can be specified: ORDER BY surname ASC, name DESC. Without ORDER BY, the result order is not guaranteed.
risposte: SORT BY column
ARRANGE BY column
ORDER BY column
GROUP BY column

cbadd4997ea7.domanda: What does the LIMIT 10 clause do in a SELECT query?
cbadd4997ea7.spiegazione: LIMIT N returns at most N rows from the result. It is often used with ORDER BY to retrieve the 'top N' records (e.g., the 10 most expensive books). In SQL Server, TOP N is used; in Oracle, ROWNUM or FETCH FIRST N ROWS ONLY is used.
risposte: Limits the total number of columns returned in the result to a maximum of 10
Returns only the first 10 rows of the result
Imposes a maximum timeout of 10 seconds on the query before forced termination
Limits the query to a maximum of 10 JOIN operations between the involved tables

715b9f02d020.domanda: What is OFFSET used for in combination with LIMIT?
715b9f02d020.spiegazione: LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20 skips the first 20 rows and returns the next 10 (rows 21-30). It is the classic mechanism for pagination: page 1 = OFFSET 0, page 2 = OFFSET 10, page 3 = OFFSET 20, etc.
risposte: Automatically excludes NULL values from the first N rows returned in the query result
Sets the starting point for ORDER BY
Skips the first N rows before applying LIMIT: used to implement pagination
Calculates the offset (distance) between column values

9d847a742d26.domanda: What is the difference between projection and selection in relational algebra applied to SQL?
9d847a742d26.spiegazione: From Codd's relational algebra: projection reduces columns (implemented with the column list in SELECT), selection/restriction reduces rows (implemented with WHERE). A typical query applies both operations.
risposte: Projection is responsible for filtering rows using WHERE, while selection filters columns using the SELECT list
Projection selects which columns to include (SELECT); selection (restriction) selects which rows to include (WHERE)
Projection and selection are synonyms in modern SQL
Projection groups rows; selection sorts them

12ce81d41633.domanda: Can the HAVING clause be used without GROUP BY?
12ce81d41633.spiegazione: HAVING without GROUP BY is valid: the entire table is treated as a single group. For example, HAVING COUNT(*) > 100 checks if the table has more than 100 rows in total. In practice, this is rare: HAVING is usually used together with GROUP BY.
risposte: No, HAVING always requires GROUP BY: it is a syntax error
Yes, HAVING without GROUP BY operates on the entire table as a single group and can filter using aggregate functions
No, HAVING requires GROUP BY and at least one JOIN
Yes, but in that case HAVING is identical to WHERE

fc18f2246992.domanda: What does the query SELECT DISTINCT nazionalita FROM autori display?
fc18f2246992.spiegazione: SELECT DISTINCT returns the list of unique nazionalita values present in the autori table, removing duplicates. If there are 50 Italian authors, 'Italiana' appears only once in the result.
risposte: All nazionalita values present in the table, including duplicate rows
The number of distinct nazionalita values as a numeric count
The distinct nazionalita values present, without repetitions
The nazionalita values sorted alphabetically with their count

40c2cdb8b3fd.domanda: What is the correct logical execution order of clauses in a SELECT query?
40c2cdb8b3fd.spiegazione: The logical execution order is: FROM (source) -> JOIN -> WHERE (row filter) -> GROUP BY -> HAVING (group filter) -> SELECT (projection) -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT. This explains why WHERE cannot use aliases defined in SELECT (as they come later).
risposte: SELECT -> FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT -> OFFSET -> FETCH
FROM -> JOIN -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT
WHERE -> FROM -> SELECT -> JOIN -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT -> OFFSET
FROM -> SELECT -> WHERE -> JOIN -> GROUP BY -> ORDER BY -> HAVING -> LIMIT -> OFFSET

564365486c03.domanda: What does the AS clause do in a SELECT statement?
564365486c03.spiegazione: AS assigns a readable alias: SELECT prezzo * 1.22 AS prezzo_con_iva. The alias does not modify the data in the table; it exists only in the query output. It is essential for calculated expressions that would otherwise have names like '?column?'.
risposte: Assigns an alias (alternative name) to a column or expression in the query result
Creates a permanent and completely independent copy of the entire table, assigning it the name specified by the user
Converts the data type of the column to the specified type
Filters rows where the value is 'as' (equal to the string)

96a39ec762a5.domanda: Does the BETWEEN 10 AND 20 operator include or exclude the boundary values?
96a39ec762a5.spiegazione: BETWEEN val1 AND val2 is equivalent to col >= val1 AND col <= val2: the boundaries are always inclusive. It works on numbers, dates, and strings (using lexicographical order). The order is important: BETWEEN 20 AND 10 will never return any rows.
risposte: It includes both: it is equivalent to >= 10 AND <= 20
It excludes both boundaries: it corresponds exactly to the condition > 10 AND < 20
It includes only the first boundary (10) but completely excludes the second boundary (20)
The behavior depends entirely on the data type defined for the affected column

11c7c3f15437.domanda: The operator IN ('Roma', 'Milano', 'Torino') is equivalent to which condition?
11c7c3f15437.spiegazione: IN (v1, v2, v3) is syntactic sugar for col = v1 OR col = v2 OR col = v3. It is more readable and scalable: if the list becomes long, IN remains clean. IN can also accept a subquery: WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM another_table).
risposte: citta LIKE 'Roma' AND citta LIKE 'Milano' AND citta LIKE 'Torino'
citta = 'Roma' AND citta = 'Milano' AND citta = 'Torino'
citta = 'Roma' OR citta = 'Milano' OR citta = 'Torino'
citta BETWEEN 'Roma' AND 'Torino'

06c19749f9bc.domanda: What does the pattern LIKE '%one%' match?
06c19749f9bc.spiegazione: The % wildcard in LIKE corresponds to any sequence of zero or more characters. '%one%' matches 'one', 'Bone', 'money', 'telefone', etc. Similarly: 'one%' matches strings that start with 'one'; '%one' matches strings that end with 'one'.
risposte: Only text strings that start exactly with the character sequence 'one'
Only text strings that end exactly with the character sequence 'one'
Any string that contains 'one' in any position
Strings consisting of exactly 5 characters total that contain 'one' in the middle

52b488e0db2a.domanda: The underscore wildcard _ in LIKE represents:
52b488e0db2a.spiegazione: The underscore _ in LIKE matches exactly one single character. For example, '198_' matches '1980', '1984', '1989', but not '19800'. '___' matches strings of exactly 3 characters. The % wildcard, on the other hand, matches sequences of any length, including empty ones.
risposte: Any sequence of zero or more characters (like %)
Exactly one single character
A numeric character (digit 0-9)
The beginning or end of the string

9d113dd8f5fd.domanda: LIKE and case-sensitivity in PostgreSQL. Which case-insensitive alternative does PostgreSQL offer?
9d113dd8f5fd.spiegazione: ILIKE is the case-insensitive variant of LIKE specific to PostgreSQL. With ILIKE, 'Italia', 'ITALIA', and 'italia' are considered equal. In MySQL, LIKE is case-insensitive by default for standard collations.
risposte: LIKE* (with asterisk)
CLIKE
ILIKE
SLIKE

a1211d0ff0a0.domanda: Given the condition WHERE eta > 18 AND citta = 'Roma' OR professione = 'Medico', how is it evaluated regarding operator precedence?
a1211d0ff0a0.spiegazione: The precedence of logical operators in SQL is: NOT > AND > OR. AND binds more tightly than OR. Therefore, the condition is evaluated as (eta > 18 AND citta = 'Roma') OR professione = 'Medico'. To change the logic, explicit parentheses are required.
risposte: (eta > 18 AND citta = 'Roma') OR professione = 'Medico'
eta > 18 AND (citta = 'Roma' OR professione = 'Medico')
eta > 18 OR (citta = 'Roma' AND professione = 'Medico')
All conditions have equal priority and are evaluated from left to right

b9623abd2ae2.domanda: What happens if you use WHERE col NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)?
b9623abd2ae2.spiegazione: In three-valued logic, col <> NULL is always UNKNOWN. If the NOT IN list contains NULL, for every row the condition becomes UNKNOWN (not TRUE), so no rows are returned. Solution: use NOT EXISTS instead of NOT IN when the subquery might produce NULL.
risposte: It works normally: it returns all rows where col is neither 1, nor 2, nor NULL
It never returns any rows, because the comparison col <> NULL is always UNKNOWN
It returns only the rows where the column col has the value IS NULL
It returns a blocking syntax error, because NULL cannot appear in an IN list

ce64f4be8350.domanda: Which query finds all authors whose name starts with 'M' or 'G'?
ce64f4be8350.spiegazione: The correct solution in standard SQL is to use OR with two separate LIKE conditions. WHERE nome LIKE '[MG]%' works in SQL Server but not in PostgreSQL (which does not support character classes in LIKE, but uses regular expressions with ~). BETWEEN would also include letters like H, I, J, K, L.
risposte: WHERE nome LIKE 'M%' OR nome LIKE 'G%'
WHERE nome IN ('M', 'G')
WHERE nome BETWEEN 'G' AND 'M'
WHERE nome LIKE '[MG]%'

898ab282f193.domanda: Does the condition BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' on a DATE column include December 31, 2020?
898ab282f193.spiegazione: BETWEEN always includes both endpoints, regardless of the data type (numbers, dates, strings). '2020-12-31' is included in the result. Note: if the column is TIMESTAMP, BETWEEN '2020-12-31' excludes hours after midnight on 12/31/2020.
risposte: No, BETWEEN always excludes the upper bound
Yes, BETWEEN always includes both endpoints
It depends on the DBMS: some include, others exclude
No, BETWEEN for dates uses exclusive intervals

5421c5c65fea.domanda: How do you correctly search for a NULL value in a SQL column?
5421c5c65fea.spiegazione: The only correct way to find NULL values is using IS NULL (or IS NOT NULL for the opposite). The comparison with = NULL always returns UNKNOWN (never TRUE) because NULL is not equal to anything, not even to itself, in SQL's three-valued logic.
risposte: WHERE column = NULL
WHERE column == NULL
WHERE column IS NULL
WHERE column <> NOT NULL

8f4d1e687170.domanda: How many rows does an INNER JOIN between table A (10 rows) and table B (8 rows) produce if no rows have a match?
8f4d1e687170.spiegazione: An INNER JOIN includes in the result ONLY the rows that have a match in both tables. If no row from table A matches any row from table B, the result is empty: 0 rows.
risposte: 80 rows (Cartesian product)
10 rows (the maximum between the two tables)
0 rows

9c42291bc85d.domanda: What does the LEFT JOIN + WHERE right_table.col IS NULL trick do?
9c42291bc85d.spiegazione: With LEFT JOIN, columns from the right table are NULL where there is no match. Filtering with WHERE right_table.col IS NULL retrieves exactly the rows without a match (anti-join). E.g., all customers without orders, all products never sold.
risposte: Identifies and returns rows from the left table that have a match in the right table
Finds rows from the left table that do NOT have a match in the right table (anti-join)
Removes NULLs from the right table
Converts the LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN

51ae06daff28.domanda: What is the result of a CROSS JOIN between a table with 6 rows and one with 7 rows?
51ae06daff28.spiegazione: A CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product: every row from the first table is combined with every row from the second. No ON condition is applied. 6 x 7 = 42 rows. Useful for generating all possible combinations (e.g., sizes x colors x models).
risposte: 42 rows (Cartesian product 6 x 7)
6 rows (the minimum between the two tables)
Depends on the specified ON condition

8168a94cccdf.spiegazione: The FULL OUTER JOIN is the combination of LEFT and RIGHT JOIN: it returns all rows from both tables. Where there is no match on one side, the columns from that side are NULL. It is rarely used, but useful for identifying 'gaps' in both directions.
risposte: Only the rows with a match in both tables
All rows from the left table, filled with NULL wherever there is no match on the right
The Cartesian product of both tables without conditions
All rows from both tables, with NULL where there is no match in either direction

92cf5476398e.domanda: In a query with multiple JOINs, does the order of tables affect the logical result?
92cf5476398e.spiegazione: For INNER JOIN, A JOIN B and B JOIN A produce the same result (logically commutative). For LEFT JOIN, the order is crucial: A LEFT JOIN B returns all rows from A; B LEFT JOIN A returns all rows from B — different results.
risposte: Yes, always: changing the order always produces different results
No for INNER JOIN (equivalent result); yes for LEFT/RIGHT JOIN where the 'main' table changes
Never: the DBMS always optimizes the order automatically
Yes, but only when using more than three tables simultaneously

eb6082840881.domanda: What is the correct ON condition in a SELF JOIN of the employees table to link each employee to their manager (the table has columns: id, name, manager_id)?
eb6082840881.spiegazione: In a SELF JOIN (FROM employees d JOIN employees m ...), d is the alias for employees, and m is the alias for managers. The correct condition is ON d.manager_id = m.id: the employee's manager_id must match the manager's id in the same table.
risposte: ON d.id = m.id
ON d.manager_id = m.manager_id
ON d.manager_id = m.id
ON d.id = m.manager_id

91da61e74492.spiegazione: A NATURAL JOIN automatically identifies columns with the same name in both tables and uses them as the join condition. It is generally discouraged in production: if a column with the same name is added to one of the tables, the join behavior changes silently.
risposte: An automatic JOIN on all columns with the same name in both tables, without an explicit ON condition
A JOIN that uses an explicit ON condition defined by the developer
A JOIN between a table and itself with two different aliases
It is a JOIN that automatically includes rows without a match, behaving like a FULL OUTER JOIN

b5710e99125a.domanda: A RIGHT JOIN between A and B is equivalent to which other type of JOIN?
b5710e99125a.spiegazione: RIGHT JOIN and LEFT JOIN are equivalent when the order of the tables is reversed. A RIGHT JOIN B = B LEFT JOIN A. For this reason, RIGHT JOIN is rarely used: it is preferred to rewrite everything as a LEFT JOIN for consistency and readability.
risposte: An INNER JOIN between A and B
Executing a complete FULL OUTER JOIN between the two tables A and B involved in the query
A LEFT JOIN between B and A (by reversing the order of the tables)
A CROSS JOIN between B and A

45f079dec804.domanda: What does the USING clause do in a JOIN?
45f079dec804.spiegazione: USING (column) is a shorthand for ON t1.column = t2.column when the column has the same name in both tables. E.g., JOIN orders USING (customer_id). The advantage is that the column appears only once in the result, not duplicated.
risposte: Replaces ON when the join condition is on columns with the same name in both tables
Specifies the table alias in the JOIN
Indicates the type of JOIN to perform (INNER, LEFT, etc.)
Filters the rows of the JOIN based on an additional condition

70bacc251a69.domanda: Which type of JOIN includes ALL rows from the left table in the result, even if there is no match in the right table?
70bacc251a69.spiegazione: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table. Where there is no match in the right table, the right table's columns are NULL. Typical use case: all customers even if they have no orders, all products even if they have never been sold.
risposte: INNER JOIN
LEFT JOIN (LEFT OUTER JOIN)
CROSS JOIN
FULL OUTER JOIN

d5058140aa61.domanda: What does the AVG(column) function do?
d5058140aa61.spiegazione: AVG(column) calculates the arithmetic mean of NON NULL values. If the column contains [10, 20, NULL, 30], AVG returns 20 (60/3, ignoring the NULL). Like all aggregate functions except COUNT(*), it ignores NULLs in the calculation.
risposte: Simply returns the maximum numeric value present in the specified column
Exclusively counts the number of rows that have a non-NULL value in the column
Returns the average value of non-NULL values in the column
Sums all values present in the column, including NULL values

34f3291cb406.domanda: Which aggregate function returns the largest value in a column?
34f3291cb406.spiegazione: MAX(column) returns the maximum value among all non-NULL values in the column. It works on numbers, strings (lexicographical order), and dates. GREATEST() is a different function: it compares multiple values row by row, not aggregating multiple rows.
risposte: GREATEST()
TOP()
UPPER()
MAX()

1438df0dadf8.domanda: If a column contains [10, 20, NULL, 30], what does AVG(column) return?
1438df0dadf8.spiegazione: AVG ignores NULL values: it calculates the sum of non-NULL values (10+20+30=60) divided by their count (3), resulting in 20. If you want to treat NULL as 0, you can use AVG(COALESCE(column, 0)), but this is semantically different.
risposte: 15 — calculates 60 divided by 4, treating NULL as 0
NULL — because there is a NULL in the list
20 — calculates 60 divided by 3, ignoring the NULL
Error: AVG cannot operate on columns with NULL values

0ea57c01271d.domanda: Which query counts the number of authors for each nationality, showing only nationalities with more than 3 authors?
0ea57c01271d.spiegazione: WHERE cannot use aggregate functions (it is executed before grouping). The filter on groups goes in HAVING. The correct structure is: GROUP BY nationality HAVING COUNT(*) > 3. WHERE nationality IS NOT NULL (without aggregates) would be valid instead.
risposte: SELECT nationality, COUNT(*) FROM authors WHERE COUNT(*) > 3 GROUP BY nationality ORDER BY 2;
SELECT nationality FROM authors GROUP BY nationality WHERE COUNT(*) > 3 ORDER BY nationality;
SELECT nationality, COUNT(*) FROM authors HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;
SELECT nationality, COUNT(*) FROM authors GROUP BY nationality HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

fa852e37fe5f.domanda: What does COUNT(*) return on a completely empty table (zero rows)?
fa852e37fe5f.spiegazione: COUNT(*) on an empty table returns 0, not NULL. This is one of the cases where an aggregation over zero rows returns a defined value (zero). Other aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN) return NULL when applied to zero rows.
risposte: NULL
Error: COUNT(*) requires at least one row

9362b9e85c8e.domanda: Do MIN and MAX also work on text (VARCHAR) columns?
9362b9e85c8e.spiegazione: MIN and MAX work on numbers, dates, AND text. For text, they use lexicographical order (collation): MIN(last_name) returns the alphabetically 'smallest' last name; MAX(last_name) returns the 'largest'. NULLs are ignored, as with all aggregate functions.
risposte: Yes, they also work on text using lexicographical (alphabetical) order
No, MIN and MAX functions can only operate on numeric data and dates
Yes, but only if an index has already been defined on the text column
No, for text values you must use the FIRST() and LAST() functions

4834c600ed2e.domanda: Which statement about SUM(column) is correct when the column contains NULL values?
4834c600ed2e.spiegazione: SUM, like all aggregate functions (except COUNT(*)), ignores NULLs. SUM([10, NULL, 30, NULL]) = 40. If you want to treat NULL as 0, use SUM(COALESCE(column, 0)). Only if ALL rows are NULL does SUM return NULL.
risposte: SUM returns NULL if even one value is NULL
SUM treats NULLs as 0 and sums them normally
SUM returns an error if it finds a NULL in the column
SUM ignores NULLs and sums only non-NULL values

a3440fbe4c9f.domanda: What does a scalar subquery do?
a3440fbe4c9f.spiegazione: A scalar subquery returns exactly one value. E.g., WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM books). If the subquery returns more than one row, the DBMS generates an error. If it returns no rows, the result is NULL.
risposte: Returns a set of rows across multiple columns usable in the FROM clause
Always refers to the current row being processed by the outer query and is executed once for each row
Returns a column of values to be used with IN or NOT IN
Returns exactly a single value (one row, one column) usable with comparison operators

36f24a66f8ec.domanda: Which type of subquery references a column from the outer query and is re-executed for each row?
36f24a66f8ec.spiegazione: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query (correlation) and is re-executed for each row of the outer query. It is typically used with EXISTS or NOT EXISTS. It can be more efficient than IN on large tables due to short-circuit evaluation.
risposte: Scalar subquery, which always returns a single atomic value
List subquery, typically used with the IN operator in the WHERE clause
Subquery in the FROM clause, i.e., a temporary derived table used as a source
Correlated subquery (used with EXISTS/NOT EXISTS)

5d1c105d46c3.domanda: When using a subquery in the FROM clause, what is mandatory to specify?
5d1c105d46c3.spiegazione: When using a subquery in the FROM clause (derived table), it is mandatory to assign it an alias: SELECT * FROM (SELECT id, name FROM authors WHERE active = TRUE) AS active_authors. Without an alias, the DBMS returns a syntax error.
risposte: The subquery must return exactly one row
An alias for the subquery
GROUP BY in the subquery
The subquery cannot contain JOINs

c6e79093db38.domanda: What is the main difference between IN and EXISTS for correlated subqueries on large tables?
c6e79093db38.spiegazione: IN executes the subquery once, collects all values, and then compares. EXISTS executes the subquery for each row but uses short-circuit evaluation: it stops as soon as it finds the first match. On large tables, EXISTS can be much more efficient.
risposte: IN is always faster than EXISTS on any table
EXISTS uses short-circuit evaluation (stops at the first match) and can be more efficient; IN collects all values first
EXISTS returns the found values; IN returns only TRUE or FALSE
There is no performance difference: the DBMS always optimizes them in the same way

e93b33c3c1ab.domanda: Why is WHERE prezzo > AVG(prezzo) not valid in SQL?
e93b33c3c1ab.spiegazione: WHERE operates on individual rows before any aggregation takes place. AVG(prezzo) is a function that operates on all rows: it cannot be calculated at the time WHERE works on a single row. The solution is to use a subquery: WHERE prezzo > (SELECT AVG(prezzo) FROM tabella).
risposte: Because AVG always requires the GROUP BY clause
Because the prezzo column must always and only be compared with a constant value
Because WHERE cannot use aggregate functions: it operates row by row before grouping
Because AVG returns NULL if there are NULL values in the column

c7363c2b423c.domanda: Which query correctly uses a scalar subquery to find the books with the maximum price?
c7363c2b423c.spiegazione: A scalar subquery must be enclosed in parentheses and used with a comparison operator. WHERE prezzo = (SELECT MAX(prezzo) FROM libri) is the correct form. Without parentheses, it is a syntax error. WHERE prezzo = MAX(prezzo) is not valid (aggregate functions are not allowed in WHERE).
risposte: SELECT * FROM libri WHERE prezzo = MAX(prezzo) GROUP BY id ORDER BY prezzo DESC;
SELECT * FROM libri WHERE prezzo > SELECT MAX(prezzo) FROM libri ORDER BY id ASC;
SELECT * FROM libri WHERE prezzo = (SELECT MAX(prezzo) FROM libri);
SELECT * FROM libri HAVING prezzo = MAX(prezzo) GROUP BY id ORDER BY id ASC;

2938aa6b1780.domanda: Does a VIEW physically store data?
2938aa6b1780.spiegazione: A standard VIEW does not physically store data. It is merely a saved query with a name. Each query on the VIEW executes the underlying query in real time. MATERIALIZED VIEWs (available in PostgreSQL), on the other hand, physically store the result and update it only upon explicit request.
risposte: Yes, it is a physical copy of the data automatically updated with every minor change in the underlying tables
No, it is a saved SQL query: data is calculated in real time every time the VIEW is queried
Yes, but only for VIEWs that use GROUP BY or aggregate functions
It depends on the DBMS: PostgreSQL stores physically, MySQL does not

d74e017721fa.domanda: How do you update the definition of an existing VIEW in PostgreSQL without having to drop it first?
d74e017721fa.spiegazione: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW nome AS SELECT ... recreates the VIEW with the new definition without needing to drop it first with DROP VIEW. Note: in PostgreSQL, OR REPLACE cannot change the types of existing columns: to do so, you must use DROP VIEW + CREATE VIEW.
risposte: UPDATE VIEW nome AS SELECT ...;
ALTER VIEW nome AS SELECT ...;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW nome AS SELECT ...;
MODIFY VIEW nome AS SELECT ...;

ecedcd77ab1e.domanda: Which of the following is an advantage of using VIEWS for security?
ecedcd77ab1e.spiegazione: A VIEW can expose only specific columns or rows of a table. The user is granted SELECT permission on the VIEW (not on the underlying table), allowing them to see only authorized data. For example, a salary VIEW that shows only their own salary, not others'.
risposte: A significantly increases query speed through physical storage and ordered data on disk
They allow granting access to filtered or partial data without exposing the underlying tables
They completely replace the need to use indexes
They automatically eliminate the need to write JOINs in queries

59569f6a2c43.domanda: What happens to the data in the underlying tables when you execute DROP VIEW name?
59569f6a2c43.spiegazione: DROP VIEW only removes the definition of the VIEW (the saved query), not the data. The underlying tables remain intact with all their data. The VIEW is just a 'window' onto the data: deleting it does not affect the actual data.
risposte: The data contained in the underlying tables is also permanently deleted along with the VIEW
The VIEW is deleted, but the data in the underlying tables remains intact
The affected data is automatically moved into a dedicated historical archive table
An error is returned: VIEWs cannot be deleted as long as there are active queries on them

916aec01326c.domanda: What does the NULL value mean in SQL?
916aec01326c.spiegazione: NULL is not zero, not an empty string, and not FALSE. NULL means that the value is unknown or not applicable. This distinction is fundamental: NULL and 0 are conceptually very different (e.g., a null salary vs. an unknown salary).
risposte: The value zero (0) is used as an automatic substitute for all numeric columns
An empty string ('') is used as an automatic substitute for text columns
The logical value FALSE is used as an automatic substitute for boolean columns
The absence of a value: the data is unknown or not applicable

c392412afc38.domanda: What is the result of the expression 5 + NULL in SQL?
c392412afc38.spiegazione: Any arithmetic operation involving NULL returns NULL. 5 + NULL = NULL, NULL * 100 = NULL, 'testo' || NULL = NULL. NULL 'propagates' through all operations.
risposte: NULL
Type error

c5bb8c3e19bb.domanda: Which SQL function returns the first non-NULL value among the arguments passed?
c5bb8c3e19bb.spiegazione: COALESCE(val1, val2, ...) returns the first non-NULL argument. E.g., COALESCE(email, 'not available') returns 'not available' if email is NULL. NVL() is specific to Oracle; ISNULL() is used in SQL Server and MySQL. COALESCE() is the SQL standard.
risposte: NULLIF()
COALESCE()
ISNULL()
NVL()

8e59236d6ad2.domanda: What does the SQL function NULLIF(a, b) do?
8e59236d6ad2.spiegazione: NULLIF(a, b) returns NULL if a = b, otherwise it returns a. Classic use case: avoiding division by zero. Example: SUM(value) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) — if COUNT(*) is 0, NULLIF returns NULL and the division results in NULL instead of an error.
risposte: Returns NULL if a is different from b, otherwise returns b
Returns NULL if a is equal to b, otherwise returns a
Checks if a or b are NULL and returns the first non-NULL value
Replaces all NULLs in column a with value b

530e61fea950.domanda: What does NULL OR TRUE return in SQL (three-valued logic)?
530e61fea950.spiegazione: In SQL's three-valued logic: NULL OR TRUE = TRUE. The reasoning is: even without knowing the first operand (NULL/UNKNOWN), if the second is TRUE, the entire OR expression is TRUE. Similarly, NULL AND FALSE = FALSE (regardless of the first operand, the second is FALSE).
risposte: NULL
FALSE
TRUE
UNKNOWN

abf1f800ef64.domanda: What does property A represent in the ACID properties?
abf1f800ef64.spiegazione: Atomicity: a transaction is an indivisible unit. There is no such thing as a 'partial commit': either all operations succeed (COMMIT) or no changes are applied (ROLLBACK). Example: a bank transfer requiring two operations — either both succeed or neither is applied.
risposte: Authentication: the transaction always verifies the connected user's credentials before proceeding
Atomicity: the transaction is an indivisible unit — either all operations succeed, or none do
Storage: data is saved permanently and redundantly to disk already during the transaction
Aggregation: all involved data is grouped and summarized immediately before the final COMMIT

7d5f6106783d.domanda: What does the D (Durability) property of ACID guarantee?
7d5f6106783d.spiegazione: Durability: once committed, the transaction is permanent. No system crash, power failure, or hardware fault can cause data loss. The DBMS uses techniques such as write-ahead logging (WAL) to ensure this property.
risposte: That data is duplicated on two separate servers for security
That each transaction is executed by a single user at a time
That changes made by a committed transaction survive even in case of crashes or hardware failures
It ensures that data is automatically deleted once a defined period of time has elapsed

faa162bb55cb.domanda: Which SQL command rolls back all operations of a transaction that has not yet been committed?
faa162bb55cb.spiegazione: ROLLBACK undoes all changes made from the start of the transaction (or since the last SAVEPOINT), restoring the database to its previous state. In PostgreSQL, ABORT can also be used as a synonym, but ROLLBACK is the SQL standard.
risposte: ROLLBACK
UNDO
ABORT TRANSACTION
REVERT

ab1c4f3dd3a3.spiegazione: SAVEPOINTs create partial rollback points: SAVEPOINT name creates the point, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT name returns to that point without rolling back everything. Useful for long and complex transactions where you want the ability to undo only part of it.
risposte: Automatic backups created by the DBMS every hour
Intermediate rollback points within a transaction: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT name returns to the savepoint state without rolling back the entire transaction
Commands to permanently save data to disk as an alternative to COMMIT
Special indexes automatically created on primary key columns

d00afe30f20e.domanda: What does the I (Isolation) property of ACID mean?
d00afe30f20e.spiegazione: Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other: a transaction does not see uncommitted changes from other concurrent transactions. The isolation level is configurable (READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE) with a trade-off between correctness and performance.
risposte: That the database can be used by only one user at a time
That data is encrypted during network transmission
That concurrent transactions execute as if they were sequential: a transaction does not see uncommitted changes from another
That each table is isolated from others: no JOINs are allowed between different tables

5ab361a1bf2a.domanda: What is the correct sequence of commands for an explicit transaction in PostgreSQL?
5ab361a1bf2a.spiegazione: The standard sequence is: BEGIN (starts the transaction), execute SQL statements (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), then COMMIT to make changes permanent or ROLLBACK to undo them all. Without an explicit BEGIN, each statement is an autonomous transaction in auto-commit mode.
risposte: START -> EXECUTE -> SAVE -> END
TRANSACTION BEGIN -> SQL -> COMMIT or ABORT
BEGIN -> SQL statements -> COMMIT (if all OK) or ROLLBACK (if error)
